member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChannelRegistry
member.summary: Plugin messaging channels (Paper's Messenger, sendPluginMessage). listens on a channel: the messages that the clients send on it arrive in the handler. The engine tells the clients which channels are listened on (minecraft:register). Send with .
member.remarks: Refused: the minecraft:* channels (a client's own registrations are read through ), velocity:* and bungeecord:*. Messages arrive in the tick window, in order per player, within the budgets of scripting.channels (a message beyond them is dropped). A listener ends with its plugin (unload or reload). Tick thread only. The worker delivers the messages; the in-process runtime does not.

The engine already listens on too many channels.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChatRoute
member.summary: Restricts who gets a chat message while its handler runs. Signed chat stays signed: a restricted line is sent to the listed players only, as the engine's own private messages are.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.ChatRoute.Restrict(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mc.Scripting.Player})
member.summary: Restricts the recipients of the chat message of the running handler. Only the listed players get the line. Works in a or a handler; the restriction applies to that one message only and ends when the dispatch is over. A second call replaces the list. An empty list means nobody gets the line. Offline handles are left out.
member.param: The players who get the message (at most 4096).
member.returns: The number of distinct recipients kept; -1 when no PlayerChat or PrivateMessage handler is running, or when the engine refuses the list.
member.exception: More than 4096 recipients. Nothing is sent to the engine.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Chat
member.summary: Chat lines that no player signed: the disguised chat the console's /say sends. The chat type picks the vanilla format and the name and message are shown in it. Use it for lines that are not a player's own words (a notice in a staff channel, a relayed message). The line is unsigned and has no signature marker, so it is never shown as a player's verified chat; for a player's own words use the chat event instead.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Chat.SendTo(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{Mc.Scripting.Player},Mc.Scripting.ChatKind,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component,Mc.Scripting.Text.Component)
member.summary: Sends an unsigned chat line to some players. The line is formatted from and (the sender's name as the line shows it) and . The message kinds (, , , ) need (the other side's name, as the vanilla format shows it); without one the call returns -1. Players who do not accept chat are skipped.
member.param: The players who get the line (at most 4096). Offline handles are left out.
The chat type of the line.
The sender name shown in the line.
The second name for a message kind; null for the others.
member.returns: The number of players the line reached; -1 when the engine refuses the call (a missing target for a message kind, an unknown kind).
member.exception: More than 4096 recipients. Nothing is sent to the engine.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.ChatMute
member.summary: Chat mutes. The engine keeps the mute table itself (it survives plugin reloads and server restarts) and refuses a muted player's chat lines, /say, /me and private messages before a plugin sees them, so a plugin does not check mutes on the message path. Commands and other actions are not affected. The reason is what the engine's mute notice (chat.mute_notice) can show the player. Thread: tick thread.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.ChatMute.Set(Mc.Scripting.Uuid,System.Nullable{System.DateTimeOffset},System.String)
member.summary: Mutes a player's chat. A mute already in force is replaced by this one; the same mute again changes nothing.
member.param: When the mute ends; null = forever.
The reason, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; null or empty for none.
member.exception: The expiry is not in the future, or the reason is longer than 256 UTF-8 bytes. Nothing is changed.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.CustomBlock
member.summary: A custom block: a state of a vanilla block that vanilla play seldom produces (and never turns a block into: the engine guards it), with its own hardness, drops and behaviour. The world stores a plain vanilla block state (so a server without the plugin shows a note block, never a corrupt chunk); a resource pack gives that state its own model ().

remarks.para: Which state. Custom blocks live in the note block's states with a mob head instrument (the ones nobody gets without a head above the block), 175 of them, handed out in registration order and remembered in the file named by content.state_file in Ramjet.toml, so the same id gets the same state after a restart. names the family: only minecraft:note_block exists in this version. While a block is registered the vanilla note block behaviour (tuning, notes, the instrument following the block below) is suppressed for its state.

Mining. The server decides how long a block takes to break, from ; the client predicts it from the note block (hardness 0.8), so a block that takes much longer than that appears to break on the client and comes back (the server refuses to finish it early): keep custom hardness near 0.8 or lower for smooth mining.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.ResourcePackBuilder
member.summary: Builds the resource pack zip that goes with custom content: item definitions, models, textures, language files and the block state remap of custom blocks. The output is deterministic (sorted entries, fixed timestamps), so the same input gives the same SHA-1 and clients keep their cached copy until something changes.

example.code: var pack = ResourcePackBuilder.Create("myplugin") .Description("My plugin") .AddItem(ruby, PackImage.Solid(0xFFE0115F)) .AddCustomBlock(rubyOre, PackImage.Checker(0xFF8B0A3C, 0xFFE0115F)) .AddLang("en_us", new Dictionary<string, string> { ["item.myplugin.ruby"] = "Ruby" }) .Build(); pack.SendTo(player); // hosted by ResourcePackHost (content.pack_host_port), or pack.ToResourcePack(yourUrl)

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Content.ResourcePackHost
member.summary: A small built-in web server that hands out the resource packs plugins publish, so a plugin needs no web space of its own. It is off until it is configured (content.pack_host_port in Ramjet.toml, with pack_host_bind and the public pack_host_url) or started by code with ; it listens on 127.0.0.1 unless told otherwise, answers only GET / HEAD of /<sha1>.zip for packs that were published, and keeps nothing of the plugins that published them (a pack is removed when its plugin unloads).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.McPluginAttribute
member.summary: The manifest of a source plugin (a .cs file or folder the server compiles at startup), written as an assembly attribute at the top of one of its files: [assembly: McPlugin("homes", version: "1.2.0", depends: ["economy >=1.0"])]. member.summary: Registers (or re-binds) a plain-data component backed by a flecs component. Keys are global ("myplugin:health"); registering the same key with the same layout (field types and offsets) after a hot reload keeps existing component values. member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.IEvent
member.summary: An event type. Catalogue events are ref structs: a handler gets the event by reference and can neither store it nor capture it in a closure or an async method, so the borrowed native data it carries (strings, byte buffers) cannot outlive the dispatch. Plugin-defined events are ordinary blittable structs that start with an field (or ref structs of the same layout).
member.remarks: Catalogue events are the engine's built-in events (fixed ids). Plugins can declare their own events: implement (e.g. "myplugin:thing") and leave at 0; an id is assigned at runtime.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerPreLoginEvent
member.summary: A client finished authentication and is about to enter the configuration phase. Handlers run on the TICK thread: a blocking call (a database or web lookup) freezes the whole server, so do not look anything up here. Cancel to refuse the login (set the kick message first), or call Defer() and answer later from Scheduler.RunAsync: the login waits up to 30 seconds, continues when every deferral allowed it and is refused as soon as one denies. A plugin that unloads releases its pending deferrals (counted as allowed).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Events.PlayerPreLoginEvent.Defer
member.summary: Holds the login until the returned is completed (up to the server's login timeout, 30 seconds). Use it to decide asynchronously (database or web lookups): call and complete the deferral from any thread. Cancelling the event instead refuses the login at once.
member.returns: The deferral to complete with or .

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Events.MenuClickEvent
member.summary: A player clicked in a custom GUI (Menu) of a plugin, after InventoryClick. Menus are locked: the click is denied (the client is resynced) unless a handler sets Allow, and a cancel always denies it. A click that could move items out of or into the menu (a slot of the menu, shift click, double click, drag, number key, off hand key) is delivered here with the slot of the menu's own numbering (top slots first, then the player's 27 + 9 slots).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Http
member.summary: HTTP(S) for plugins. In the plugin worker the requests are performed by the server: its HTTP client resolves each name, refuses loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses, limits request and response sizes and the rate, and enforces the timeouts (see the server's scripting.http.* settings in ramjet.toml). In an in-process host (development only) requests go out directly. Use , or new HttpClient(Http.Handler) for your own timeouts and headers. Do not dispose either: they are shared by every plugin.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Http.Handler
member.summary: The message handler behind every request. Share it; do not dispose it.

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Http.Client
member.summary: A shared client over . Set the time limit per request with a ; the server applies its own total timeout as well. Do not dispose it.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.IInventory
member.summary: A list of item slots: a player's inventory, a chest, a plugin menu. Every read returns a copy of the stack in the slot and every write replaces the stack: no object aliases the engine's storage, so a stack can be kept and a slot can change under it without harm. Slots count from 0. Tick thread only.

member.summary: Every slot in order (a snapshot).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.EngineInventory
member.summary: Shared implementation of the inventories the engine owns: one native call per operation, the inventory is addressed by (kind, world, reference) every time, so a handle never keeps anything alive and a block that was destroyed meanwhile simply reads as an empty inventory.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.PlayerInventory
member.summary: The inventory of a player: 41 slots numbered like the game's own inventory container, plus the cursor. Slots 0-8 are the hotbar, 9-35 the main inventory, 36 to 39 the armor (boots, leggings, chestplate, helmet) and 40 the off hand. member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.ItemStack
member.summary: An immutable item stack value: an item type, a count and data components. Every With... method returns a new stack; the value can be kept, compared and put into inventories, menus and the world (, , ).

remarks.para: Components are addressed by their registry key ("minecraft:custom_name") and carry NBT values. The ones the server converts are given in a plugin friendly form: text components (custom_name, item_name, lore lines) as JSON strings (what makes), integers (damage, max_damage, max_stack_size, repair_cost, map_id, enchantable, dyed_color), rarity as "common" .. "epic", enchantment_glint_override as a byte, unbreakable / glider as an empty compound, custom_data as a compound, item_model and tooltip_style as identifier strings, custom_model_data as {floats, flags, strings, colors}, enchantments and stored_enchantments as {"minecraft:sharpness": 3}, tooltip_display as {hide_tooltip, hidden_components}, use_cooldown as {seconds, group?} and food as {nutrition, saturation, can_always_eat}. Every other component the server knows is read as an opaque byte array holding its network encoding: it survives copying a stack but cannot be edited. A component key starting with ! removes a component of the item's prototype ().
A stack that no inventory accepts (unknown item, a count above the stack size, a component whose value does not convert) is refused by the call that receives it with an .

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.MenuClick
member.summary: A click in a . A menu is locked: a click that could move items out of the menu or into it (a slot of the menu, shift click, double click, number key, the off hand key, the drop key, a middle click) is denied and the client is resynced unless the handler calls ; always denies. Clicks that only touch the player's own inventory slots pass unless a handler cancels them (or the menu locks the player inventory too). The object is valid during the handler only.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Inventories.Menu
member.summary: A custom GUI: a container with icons and click handlers that the client shows like a chest, a hopper or a dispenser. The menu is owned by the plugin and closed for every viewer when the plugin unloads or reloads.

remarks.para: A menu is locked. The engine keeps it a display: a click that could take an icon out or put an item in is denied (and the whole menu resynced to the client) unless a handler allows it with ; drags over its slots, shift clicks, double clicks, number keys, the off hand key and the drop key cannot move items out of it or into it; the creative clone click gives no copy of an icon. Whatever a handler decides, the server is authoritative: it only performs what vanilla would perform for the click, and a cancelled click changes nothing.

Create menus with (plugin.Menus) or the static factories, which belong to the plugin whose code is running (OnEnable, an event handler, a command, a scheduled task); items in the slots are ordinary stacks, so the menu doubles as a small shared inventory (, ).

member.summary: The packet's index in the engine's catalogue (its class has the constant Index).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus
member.summary: What did with the packet.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus.Sent
member.summary: The packet is in the player's stream, in order with the engine's packets of the tick.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus.Refused
member.summary: The packet was refused: a value out of range, an unknown registry id, an entity id this plugin may not name, or a packet the engine does not send to players.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus.NotInPlay
member.summary: The player is not in play (nothing was sent).

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus.OverBudget
member.summary: The player's (or the server's) byte budget for plugin packets of this tick is spent (nothing was sent).

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketSendStatus.NotAvailable
member.summary: The engine does not carry packets here (the in-process runtime, a test fixture): nothing was sent.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.PacketMode
member.summary: How a packet handler is called (see ).

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketMode.Observe
member.summary: A copy of the packet after the fact: the handler cannot change or cancel it, and nothing waits for it.

member.name: F:Mc.Scripting.PacketMode.Intercept
member.summary: The handler runs before the packet goes on and may cancel it or change its fields. The engine waits for the answer within a small budget; when none comes in time the packet goes on unchanged.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent`1
member.summary: One packet handed to a handler. In intercept mode the handler may change and call .

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent`1.Packet
member.summary: The packet. Changing its fields changes what goes on (the engine validates the new values like any other).

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent`1.Player
member.summary: The player the packet is from (serverbound) or to (clientbound).

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent`1.Cancelled
member.summary: True once a handler cancelled the packet.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent`1.Cancel
member.summary: Stops the packet: a serverbound packet's handler does not run, a clientbound packet is not sent. Only in intercept mode; an observer's cancel is ignored.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Packets
member.summary: Typed packets: send a packet to a player, and observe, change or cancel the packets players send and the ones sent to them. The engine encodes every packet with its own codecs, so nothing malformed reaches a client.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Packets.On``1(System.Action{Mc.Scripting.PacketEvent{``0}},Mc.Scripting.PacketMode,Mc.Scripting.EventPriority)
member.summary: Subscribes to one packet type. In the handler sees a copy of each packet; in it may cancel the packet or change its fields. Handlers run in priority order (lowest first). Returns the subscription: dispose it to unsubscribe (also done when the plugin unloads).
member.exception: The packet cannot be observed or intercepted (its catalogue row has no such hook).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Packets.Send(Mc.Scripting.Player,Mc.Scripting.PacketBase)
member.summary: Sends a packet to a player. The packet is encoded by the engine, after the engine checks its values (ranges, registry ids, entity ids: an entity a plugin creates needs ). It is written in order with the engine's own packets of the tick.

member.summary: Raised when permissions changed (the player's id, or null when a group or everything changed): the server refreshes the command trees.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider
member.summary: The built-in backend: groups (weighted, inheriting, with prefix and suffix) and per-player overrides, stored in permissions.json. Resolution order: the player's own entries, then his groups by weight (highest first, parents after their child), then the implicit "default" group everybody belongs to. Within one layer the most specific node wins: an exact entry beats a.b.*, a longer wildcard beats a shorter one, * comes last; a false value is a denial. A key written as "-node" in the file means the same as "node": false.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Opens (and creates, when missing) the permission file. A file that cannot be read (malformed JSON) does not stop the server: the provider starts empty (the registered defaults apply), logs the problem once and leaves the file alone so that it can be fixed and reloaded with .

member.name: P:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.LoadError
member.summary: Why the file could not be read (null when it was, or since it was fixed and reloaded).

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.Reload
member.summary: Re-reads the file (a missing file is created with a "default" and an "admin" group).
member.exception: The file is not valid JSON; the permissions in memory stay as they were.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.FilePermissionProvider.Save
member.summary: Writes the file if something changed. The engine writes it (a host call: the worker's sandbox refuses writes to the server folder), atomically (temp file, flushed, then renamed over the old one). The engine refuses a write that comes too soon after the last one (its rate limit): then the changes stay pending and the next call (the runtime's flush, a second later) tries again. Never throws; a refusal is logged once per streak.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.NativePermissionTable
member.summary: Feeds the engine's permission table: declares node defaults, sets and changes the rules of a player, claims the table, and reads its statistics. The engine validates every message as a whole; a refused message changes nothing (the status is the host call's: 0 applied, -1 malformed, -2 oversize, -3 refused, -4 version gap, -5 unknown kind). While a claim is held the engine answers the permission requirements of commands from the table; the rules describe a player's permissions, and a player whose rules were never sent gets the defaults.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Permissions.PermissionManager
member.summary: The server's permission system: declared nodes with defaults, the active backend () and the question "does this player have this node?". The default backend is a on permissions.json; a plugin may replace it.
member.remarks: Resolution: the provider's explicit value (wildcards, groups and player overrides are its business); if it has no opinion, the node's registered default decides ( and friends are evaluated against the player's vanilla operator level); an unregistered node without an entry is denied, except minecraft.command.<name> which defaults to the vanilla operator level of that command. The console always has every permission. Everything here runs on the tick thread.

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Player
member.summary: A handle to a connected player. Blittable (usable in events and ECS components).
member.remarks: A handle stays valid only while the player is online: after he leaves it goes stale. Stale handles fail safe: reads return defaults, actions do nothing (see ). A player who rejoins gets a new handle. All members must be called on the tick thread.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Player.SendPluginMessage(System.String,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Sends a plugin message to the player on a channel (a custom payload of the play state). Vanilla clients ignore channels they did not register; clients with a mod or a proxy that listens on it receive the bytes.
member.param: A channel id, namespace:path. The minecraft:*, velocity:* and bungeecord:* channels are refused.
member.returns: True when the message was queued for the player; false when it was not sent: the player is not online, the channel is invalid or reserved, the payload is too large, or the tick's send budget is spent (scripting.channels.send_bytes_per_tick).

member.name: T:Mc.Scripting.Services.IPlaceholders
member.summary: The placeholder registry: text templates such as "Online: %server_online%" are rendered through it, and any plugin can add its own placeholders (the chat format, the tab list, nametags, kits, the messages of other plugins). Process-wide: the built-in instance is registered with , so every plugin in the same process sees the same names. Rendering is pure managed code (no engine call of its own): a value that reads engine state pays for that read, which is why each placeholder declares how long its value may be reused. Thread: tick thread (the values are evaluated where the text is rendered).

A registration with the same id replaces the earlier one (a hot-reload successor). Disposing the result (or unloading the owning plugin, when it registered from a plugin's enable or event handler) removes it.
member.param: The placeholder id, namespaced by its owner ("tab_ping", "essentials_balance").
How long a value may be reused. Zero evaluates it every time it is rendered.

member.name: M:Mc.Scripting.Worlds.World.SpawnEntity(System.String,Mc.Scripting.Vec3d,Mc.Scripting.Nbt.NbtCompound,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Spawns an entity of a type, like /summon. Mobs the engine simulates (zombies, cows, creepers ...) get their normal spawn logic: with no NBT their random attributes and equipment are rolled; with NBT the data is applied as given ({Health:5f,CustomName:'"Bob"'}). Item entities (minecraft:item with Item:{id:"minecraft:diamond",count:3}) and experience orbs (minecraft:experience_orb with Value) are supported too. The spawn fires (reason Plugin) where the entity kind has that event, and a handler may cancel it.
member.param: The entity type key, "minecraft:zombie" (the namespace may be left out).
The initial yaw in degrees (an NBT Rotation overrides it).
member.returns: The entity (a handle: check before keeping it), or when the type is unknown or cannot be spawned here (a type the engine does not simulate yet, the chunk is not loaded, a monster in peaceful, a handler cancelled it).

member.param: The radius-like strength (TNT is 4, a creeper 3, a charged creeper 6; the work grows with its cube, so values above 32 are refused).
Whether fires start in the explosion's wake.
Whether blocks are destroyed (false: only the entities are affected).
The entity that causes it (excluded from the damage, used as the damage source), or none.
member.returns: True when the explosion happened; false for a power outside 0-32 (exclusive of 0), an unloaded centre or an unknown world.
